questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore a different, European culture, and I wished for it to be more different from the Danish culture than I expected it would be in the more Northern parts of Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not as easy as I could've wished for. The university website wasn't that straight forward and it didn't always work well with the translation of the website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not that much

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: This is very much depending on the recommendations. We didn't have the greatest experince with "Italianway".

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The metro works well and is cheap! And Milan is not that big of a city, so walking works as well. Also, a lot of the students who went at the same time as me rented bikes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No registration (until exams), you just show up. Also they are no limits on numbers of attendees. If you change courses a little down the way you should probably just let the professors know, and ask if you have to do anything in regards of getting up to speed or if lack of attendance (in the period you did another course) is going to be a problem.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You show up to class and register for each seminar. Attendance matter. As said, if you change course a little down the way, let the professor, who's course you're changing to, know and ask if you have to do anything, read up on anything, and how you're going to work out attendance.
Registration for exams happen on the website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can ask the professors

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Had no problem with registration

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to know when to register for exams and do it as soon as possible. The system isn't as set as we know it, so registration can be stressfull. Example: the window of registration could be rather short because you have to register at least 10 days before exam, but maybe registration would not open unitl 14 days before.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not the most challenging academically, but made room for exploring the culture and country that much more.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a lot of listening. Sometimes, the level of english could cause misunderstandings until you figure out their pronunciation. Most part of the courses I attended had litlle syllabus.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It compares the most to our lectures (forelæsninger), rather than our seminars. The professors will do a lot of talking but will also encourage you to participate throughout classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Access to justice in a multilevel constitutional system
Public and Private Partnerships
Negotiation, mediation and sustainable conflict resolution
Law, culture and development in a global world
Smart cities, artificial intelligens and digital transformation law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend "Negotiation, mediation and sustainable conflict resolution". It gives you knowledge and experience you can use in the future and is also a very hands on course due to the simulations you have to do.

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping was more expensive than I expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Erasmus did social activities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on trips in different parts of Italy

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Do trips to different parts of Italy, close and further away.
Also, explore the Duomo, go to museums, go on walks, Milan is not that big so walking around great parts of the city is do-able within a weekend

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid. Reach out - and ask for help if you need it. Also, the Negotiation course (mentioned above) did a really good job at mixing people at the simulation which made us talk to other people

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The lack of structure and the way the standards are lower.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the way of embracing life

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You WILL pass, so enjoy the stay.
Make sure to register for exams on time!
Attendance MATTER, make sure to show up to be registered for classes, else you might not register for exams

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Can't think of any

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships across boarders

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The lack of structure

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
